about.text: The most protein-rich milk protein powder: skim milk ultrafiltered and diafiltered until at least 89.5 % of the powder (ADPI definition; commonly sold as 90 % or more) is milk protein, with casein and whey proteins still in roughly their milk ratio. It cannot be made by mixing separately produced caseinate and whey protein. Used to fortify high-protein bars and heat-treated (UHT) drinks.

links.name: American Dairy Products Institute: Milk protein isolate (MPI)

how.text: An MPI is made like an MPC but with much more diafiltration: the more water that washes through the membrane, the more of the lactose and minerals leave and the closer the protein comes to 90 %. Microfiltered variants exist whose casein:whey ratio is shifted (82:18 to 95:5), but those are not the standard MPI.
